pretest.enonce: Is an email with no spelling mistakes necessarily legitimate?
pretest.enonceFalc: Is a message with no mistakes always a real message?

choix.texte: Yes, criminals always make mistakes
No, AI lets criminals write flawless messages

pretest.explication: Thanks to generative AI, fraudulent messages are now polished and personalised. The absence of mistakes proves nothing.

pretest.enonce: Can a QR code lead you to a fraudulent website?
pretest.enonceFalc: Can a QR code open a fake website?

choix.texte: Yes
No, QR codes are safe

pretest.explication: A QR code is just a hidden link. It is called “quishing” when it leads to a fraudulent page.

pretest.enonce: You receive a suspicious message. What is the best reflex?
pretest.enonceFalc: You receive a strange message. What do you do?

choix.texte: Delete it without telling anyone
Report it to the security team
Forward it to colleagues to get their opinion

pretest.explication: Reporting lets the security team block the campaign for everyone. Forwarding the message spreads the risk.

posttest.enonce: Which of these are signs of phishing? (several answers possible)
posttest.enonceFalc: Which signs show a fake message? (several answers)

choix.texte: A threat to delete the account within 24 hours
A request to enter your password
The message is addressed to you by name
A sender address imitating the organisation's

posttest.explication: Urgency, a request for credentials and an imitated sender are classic signs. Being called by your name proves nothing: that information is easy to find.

posttest.enonce: An email asks you to scan a QR code to “reactivate your two-factor authentication”. What do you do?
posttest.enonceFalc: An email asks you to scan a QR code. What do you do?

choix.texte: I scan it with my personal phone, it's less risky
I don't scan it and I report the email
I reply to the sender to check

posttest.explication: Scanning with a personal phone is even riskier: it is less protected. Replying to the sender means talking to the fraudster.

posttest.enonce: You entered your password on a page that now looks suspicious. What do you do?
posttest.enonceFalc: You gave your password on a fake website. What do you do?

choix.texte: Nothing, to avoid trouble
I alert the security team immediately
I wait and see if anything happens

posttest.explication: Every minute counts: the security team can block the account and change the password before the attacker uses it. Contact: {{contacts.securite}}.

posttest.enonce: On a parking meter, a QR code is printed on a sticker placed over the official poster. What is the right attitude?
posttest.enonceFalc: A QR code is stuck on a poster. It looks added. What do you do?

choix.texte: I scan it, it's faster
I don't scan it and use the official app or website

posttest.explication: A sticker placed over an official poster is a classic sign of quishing.
